rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`. The requirement lets a skill link to files for specialized material. It requires each such link to say when to read the file. The file has three links of this kind, and each one says when to read its target:
- `[CI example](references/ci.md)` says to use it "when adding these steps to an existing workflow". The sentence before it gives the situation: setting up or reviewing project CI.
- `[references/distributed-requirements.md]` is introduced by "For an obligation that applies separately at each of many sites…", with "read … before drafting it, and whenever you edit a `{req}` that contains `{sites}` or `{violations}`".
- `[references/syntax-details.md]` is introduced by "If a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a comment, such as a shipped skill or a stylesheet… or a requirement lives in a nested chapter, read …".

The mention of `references/fixme.md` is a code span, not a link. It sits inside a sentence that says `{fixme}` acknowledges a deferred gap, and it belongs to another skill. Even if it counted as a link, that sentence gives the situation for reading it.

No violation matches were listed. I found no link that lacks a "when to read" condition.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
